rules.description: The bar's volume is at or above an absolute floor — a share or contract count, not a ratio. Brooks's liquidity / eligibility gate. Identical both sides.

catalog_match.note: both catalog volume rules measure volume against its own N-bar average; this is an absolute floor with no window at all

rules.merge_notes: One threshold test at four scales: 3M and 5M shares for daily stock selection, 25,000 and 100,000 Emini contracts intraday. Default 3,000,000; the input is instrument-specific either way. Register: the engine's `volume` is UP-TICKS, so an absolute count must read `ticks`.

rules.description: The bar's volume is at least K times its own N-bar average volume — Brooks's reversal-bar confirmation. Identical both sides.

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule is exactly this test and already reads total ctx.Ticks (up + down) rather than the up-tick `volume` alias, which is what Brooks means

rules.merge_notes: RP1-11 (stray from bar_anatomy_reversal_signal) is the catalog rule verbatim: reversal-bar volume at 5 to 10 times the 20-bar average. Do not author again. The same test recurs six more times in the breakouts_volume_gap bucket, merged there under the same key. Folded the breakouts_volume_gap copy (R00-57, R02-02, V00-42, T00-25, T00-23, V07-14): the same volume-vs-average-volume test. Book multiples differ by use - RP1-11 wants ~5x for reversal-bar confirmation, the breakout/climax sources quote up to 10x - so volumeMultiple carries both; default 5.

rules.description: The bar's volume is at or below a fraction of its own N-bar average volume — Brooks's 'quiet, low-volume market' gate. Identical both sides.

catalog_match.note: VolumeBelowAverage is this rule at volumeFraction = 1.0 with a strict <; the cheapest fix is to add a fraction input to the existing rule rather than author a second file

rules.merge_notes: Only the volume half of T06-24 is carried; its shaved-bar cluster count belongs to bar_anatomy. Brooks says only that 'the volume is low' — the 0.8 fraction is the miner's reading, not a book number. Register: `volume` is up-ticks, so this is an up-tick ratio.

rules.description: After a recent volume peak, the bar makes a lower low than the previous bar on volume well below that peak — Brooks's volume divergence, a pullback-long signal in a bear trend; mirrored for shorts.
rules.pseudocode: peakVolume = highest(volume, lookback)[1]; low[0] < low[1] && volume[0] < divergenceFraction * peakVolume

complexity.reason: a bounded Highest over the volume series stands in for remembering the climax bar; no persistent state

rules.merge_notes: Stray from swing_structure. Brooks's 'remember the huge-volume bar' is mechanized as highest(volume, lookback)[1], which needs no state; 'one or two lower lows on less volume' becomes a single lower-low bar. divergenceFraction 0.5 and lookback 5 are the miner's readings.

dropped.reason: composition of VolumeAboveAverageMultiple + a strong bull trend-bar body test (bar_anatomy) + an assumed prior-bear-trend context that the candidate never defines

design_decisions.topic: which volume series Brooks's volume rules read
options: the engine's `volume` alias, which EL_FEATURES records as UP-TICKS only (VERIFIED against 18,203 @KW bars)
`ticks`, up + down, as the catalog's VolumeAboveAverageMultiple already uses
design_decisions.recommended: `ticks` — Brooks always means total contracts or shares traded, and the catalog rule already reads ctx.Ticks; reading `volume` would silently roughly halve every absolute threshold and shift every ratio

bucket_summary: Five candidates plus three strays, collapsed to four rules. Four of the eight are one absolute-volume floor stated at four instrument scales (3M/5M shares daily, 25k/100k Emini contracts intraday), now MinimumAbsoluteVolume. RP1-11 is a straight duplicate of the catalog's VolumeAboveAverageMultiple and is marked D. V10-01 dropped as a composite. The A-list is MinimumAbsoluteVolume and VolumeBelowAverageFraction (the latter really wants a fraction input added to the existing VolumeBelowAverage rather than a new file); VolumeDivergenceAfterClimax is B. Every rule here is gated on the one design decision: the engine's `volume` is up-ticks, not total volume.
